Clean pass with one real caveat: item_text is COMPOSED, not transcribed. rr98's items are pixel-array stimuli, so there is no administered per-item wording in any source; each item_text names the stimulus strength level and its white-pixel proportion, built from rtdists rr98.Rd's definition of the strength variable, and the proportion k/32 is arithmetic on "33 equally spaced proportions from zero to 1" rather than a figure printed anywhere. Secondary caveat: resp is trial accuracy (data/rr98.R: resp <- ifelse(correct,1,0)), not the participant's dark/light key press, and correct_response is necessarily blank because the correct answer for a given strength varies trial to trial with which of the two overlapping distributions the stimulus was drawn from. Not a block; retry test not applicable. STEP 5c -- AUDIT WARN EXPLAINED: audit_batch.R flags 'row-count anomaly (possible item-code conflation or missingness skew), median=378'. Expected, and NOT an itemtext defect nor a defect in the response data. Per-item n runs from 37 (i 32) to 690 (i 15) because the item IS the stimulus strength level and Ratcliff & Rouder sampled the 33 levels non-uniformly, concentrating trials near the ambiguous midpoint where the psychometric function is informative and sampling the saturated extremes lightly. The distribution is mid-peaked and symmetric, exactly as the design implies. verify_rr98_accuracy.R reproduces every per-item n from the CRAN source data with max |n diff| = 0, so no row is missing or conflated: the skew is the experiment.
